560: I shout 'buy' and 'sell' all day. Now I shout them at home too, at the soup.
561: My reflexes are stuck from the trading floor. I nearly bought a passing pigeon this morning.
562: I've spent so long yelling numbers that I greeted my own mother with a price.
563: Buy, sell, buy, sell. I do it so fast I sometimes sell things I quite liked.
564: The floor is loud. I am loud. When I go quiet, people ask if something is wrong.
565: I raised my hand to wave hello and accidentally agreed to a very large deal.
566: My hands move faster than my thoughts. Some days I trade before I have fully woken up.
567: I shout all day at the exchange. My voice has two settings now: loud and slightly less loud.
568: I sold, then bought, then sold again, all before breakfast. Breakfast was not for sale.
569: My reflexes never switch off. I flinched at a falling leaf as if it were terrible news.
570: I buy high, sell higher, and shout the whole time. My throat files a complaint every evening.
571: On the floor I never stop moving. At dinner my hand still signals for prices no one is offering.
572: I've shouted 'sold' so often that I once said it when a waiter cleared my plate.
573: Fast hands, loud voice, quick decisions. Choosing what to have for lunch, though, takes me an hour.
574: I trade all day at full speed. When I finally sit still, the whole room feels too slow.
575: Somebody sneezed and my hand shot up to make an offer. Old habits are very fast habits.
576: I yell buy, I yell sell, I yell it with my whole chest. Quiet rooms make me deeply nervous.
577: My reflexes are so trained that I once made a bid at my own reflection. It did not accept.
578: All day it is prices and shouting. By evening I can only whisper, and I still whisper numbers.
579: I make a hundred snap decisions before noon. Then I cannot decide which chair to sit in.
580: I run notes across the whole city on foot. I have met every hill in it, personally.
581: I have the fastest legs in town and, by a wide margin, the sorest feet.
582: I ran three notes across the city before noon. Then I looked around for a fourth, out of pure habit.
583: My job is to run and not read. I have carried a thousand secrets, and kept every one unread.
584: I know every street, every shortcut, every stray dog by name. The dogs, sadly, do not know mine.
585: I delivered a note so fast the sender was still writing the next one when I got back.
586: People say I fly across town. I do not. I run. My feet would like this clearly noted.
587: I've run this city end to end so often I could do it with my eyes closed. I have not tried.
588: My legs never tire. My feet, however, hold a grudge that grows a little bigger each day.
589: I carry messages, not opinions. I once delivered an insult and a love note in one trip, at the same speed.
590: I once raced a rider on a horse across town. I lost. But I looked far more determined about it.
591: I have a perfect memory for doorways and none for faces. I reach the right house and greet the wrong person.
592: I run all day and rest by walking slowly. My idea of a relaxing holiday is a gentle jog.
593: I've worn out more shoes than I can count. The shoes gave up. My legs did not.
594: I delivered forty notes today. I remember every single route and not one single word.
595: They call me the fastest in the city. I have never slowed down enough to see if it is true.
596: I run so much that when I finally sit down, my legs keep going without me for a moment.
597: I've crossed this city so many times I recognize the cobblestones one by one.
598: My whole trade is speed. I am so used to hurrying that now I eat, sleep, and think quickly too.
599: I carried an urgent note across town in record time. It said 'no reply needed.' They always do.
